standard_prerequisites.name: A pseudo-coherent complex over A = R[x_1, ..., x_d]/I with A flat over R is pseudo-coherent as a complex of R[x_1, ..., x_d]-modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces to the polynomial presentation ring.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a map R_p -> A_q of local rings with A_q a quotient of a regular local ring, a pseudo-coherent complex whose fibre has cohomology confined to [a, b] is perfect with tor amplitude in [a - d, b]
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the perfectness and the shifted tor amplitude over A_q.

standard_prerequisites.name: A flat ring map pushes tor amplitude bounds through: a perfect complex over A_q with tor amplitude in [a - d, b] over A_q has tor amplitude in [a - d, b] over R_p
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers the tor amplitude down to R.

core_obligations: By the more-relative-pseudo-coherent-is-moot lemma K is pseudo-coherent as a complex of R[x_1, ..., x_d]-modules, so we may assume A = R[x_1, ..., x_d] with I = 0 (proof lines 22193-22195). Applying the perfect-over-regular-local-ring lemma to the local map R_p -> A_q and K_q, whose fibre cohomology is confined to [a, b] by hypothesis, K_q is perfect in D(A_q) with tor amplitude in [a - d, b] (proof lines 22196-22199). The map R_p -> A_q is flat since A is flat over R, so the flat-push-tor-amplitude lemma gives that K_q has tor amplitude in [a - d, b] over R (proof lines 22200-22201).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to A = R[x_1, ..., x_d] by relative pseudo-coherence (proof lines 22193-22195).
Get perfectness with shifted tor amplitude at the prime, then push down along the flat map (proof lines 22196-22201).
